questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: If you must stop quickly in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Brake hard on both brakes while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you need to stop quickly in a curve, first straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly. Reduce your lean angle, then press harder on the brakes as you slow down.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or place them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads against the back of the seat or frame. This raises the center of gravity and affects balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. You are more likely to notice tire failure by how the motorcycle feels and handles.

questions.question: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane because:

options.text: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
You may prevent another vehicle from passing you.
The side near the passing vehicle is safer.
You may experience a strong wind blast from the far side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not ride on the far side of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may require you to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: Studies show that most crash-involved riders:

options.text: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and do not brake the rear tire enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not use enough front brake pressure and use too much rear brake pressure.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to be done safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that inform drivers of road rules, such as speed limits, are usually rectangular and white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When someone passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay in the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle can be dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by three main factors: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. You do not need more distance if you can already see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When riding in a lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust:
questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks to handle this extra weight. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help if needed.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Riding in cool, windy, or rainy weather.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool, windy, or rainy weather.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Limit riding to about six hours per day and take breaks every two hours. Avoid stimulants, as fatigue can return suddenly when they wear off.

questions.question: At night, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds of following distance. You may need extra time to realize the vehicle ahead has stopped and to brake.

questions.question: When rain starts, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is especially slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the safest option.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When leaning in a curve, your tires have less grip than when upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: How do you get the strongest braking power?

options.text: Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time for the strongest braking power. Do not lock either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when turning left?

options.text: Push both handgrips at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean the right way, push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Ride slowly next to the dog.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, shift down and approach it slowly. Then speed up to leave the dog behind.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Park at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Park like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
Park at the left side of the space so drivers can see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb. Touch your rear wheel to the curb.

questions.question: What should you do in a slow, tight turn?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans. This balances the lean.
